meta.note: The merged functional inventory. Two corpora existed and barely overlapped: functional-english.json carried DISCURSIVE language (advantages, cause, effect, trends) for essays and reports; functions-corpus.json carried INTERACTIONAL language (thanking, inviting, refusing, advising) for letters and speaking. Seven functions collided and were folded together; the rest are complementary, which is why the merge nearly doubles coverage rather than deduplicating it. FUNCTION is the unit and the browsing axis — a learner looking for a way to disagree politely should not have to know it lives in the essays folder. Categories group the carousel; they do not gate it.
meta.phraseNote: Two phrase shapes, deliberately. Discursive phrases carry a `connector` as well as a stem — 'A major advantage of …' + 'is that it allows people to …, which means …' — because an essay sentence is built in two halves. Interactional phrases are complete as they stand.
meta.registerNote: `register` is set on phrases from functions-corpus and null on those from functional-english, which was never tagged. A card should show the informal-to-formal bar only when its phrases are graded, and a plain list otherwise: showing an axis that is not there would be a lie. Tagging the rest is authoring, and can be done one function at a time.
meta.tasksNote: A task is a QUESTION and the six cues that answer IT. Previously a question had one matching cue and the page padded the orbit with five from elsewhere in the function, so five of the six cards on screen answered a different question. Nesting the cues inside the task makes that impossible.
meta.categoryNote: Four functions were re-homed: trends had been left in `comparison` while the category named after it held none; complaining, praising and recommending arrived with the expanded set and fell to the `informational` default. Each carries a categoryNote with the reasoning.
